newsitem.title: UK: KAL to up ex-UK to Seoul rate from Nov 1.
newsitem.headline: KAL to up ex-UK to Seoul rate from Nov 1.

text.p: Korean Airlines Ltd (KAL) is planning an increase in air cargo rates of five pence per kg from 1 November ex-UK to Korea, the airline's UK cargo manager, Frank Smith told Reuters.
This "small increase" will raise the general rate per kg for 100 kg shipments to 2.05 stg, he added.
The upward movement comes against a background of strong two-way trade between Korea and the UK, and rapidly rising Korean investment in Britain.
The airline is also tentatively considering the introduction next April of a second weekly freighter -- a Boeing 747-400 -- between the two countries to cope with the growing demand, he added.
Earlier KAL said it was dropping plans for a 5 to 10 percent rise in autumn air cargo rates rise from mainland Europe due to competition.
Smith said that overall the whole Europe region, including the UK, is expected to be close to its target of 10 percent growth for 1996, despite the weakness of the continental European economies.
"As for the UK, we are taking out more than we are bringing in, although there is a strong inward demand for consumer goods," he added.
But this consumer market has not yet recovered in mainland Europe, Smith said.

Marks and Spencer Plc is seeking nine pallets a week for regular shipments of clothing to Korea, and a mockup of a small jetliner was recently shipped for the Seoul air show, he added. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
